achelousaurus:eswiki:10.title: Achelousaurus horneri (Las expediciones de Horner a Landslide Butte)

achelousaurus:eswiki:18.title: Achelousaurus horneri (Función de la gola del cuello)

facts.statement: The species of Achelousaurus is named Achelousaurus horneri.
facts.quote: species: horneri

facts.statement: The genus Achelousaurus was described by Scott D. Sampson in 1994.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Sampson, 1994

facts.statement: Achelousaurus lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 77 to 74.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: lived during the Late Cretaceous Period of what is now North America, about 77 to 74.8 million years ago

facts.statement: The first fossils of Achelousaurus were collected in Montana in 1987.
facts.quote: The first fossils of Achelousaurus were collected in Montana in 1987

facts.statement: Achelousaurus was a large centrosaurine dinosaur, estimated to be about 6 meters long and weigh 3 metric tons.
facts.quote: A large centrosaurine, Achelousaurus supposedly was about 6 m long, with a weight of about 3 MT

facts.statement: The skull of Achelousaurus featured a bony frill with a pair of long spikes that curved outward.
facts.quote: It had a bony neck-frill at the rear of the skull, which sported a pair of long spikes, which curved towards the outside

facts.statement: Adult Achelousaurus possessed rough, roundish bosses above the eyes and on the snout.
facts.quote: Adult Achelousaurus had rough bosses (roundish protuberances) above the eyes and on the snout

facts.statement: Researchers hypothesize that the bosses on Achelousaurus were used for head-butting fights and display.
facts.quote: Some researchers hypothesize that the bosses were used in fights, with the animals butting each other's heads, as well as for display

facts.statement: Achelousaurus belongs to the clade Pachyrostra, meaning "thick-snouts", within the Ceratopsia.
facts.quote: Within the Ceratopsia, Achelousaurus lies within the clade Pachyrostra (or "thick-snouts")

facts.statement: Achelousaurus fossils are found in the Two Medicine Formation, where it lived on the island continent of Laramidia.
facts.quote: Achelousaurus is known from the Two Medicine Formation and lived in the island continent of Laramidia

facts.statement: As a ceratopsian, Achelousaurus was a herbivore with a high metabolic rate.
facts.quote: As a ceratopsian, Achelousaurus would have been a herbivore and it appears to have had a high metabolic rate

facts.statement: All known specimens of Achelousaurus were recovered from the Two Medicine Formation in Glacier County, Montana.
facts.quote: All known Achelousaurus specimens were recovered from the Two Medicine Formation in Glacier County, Montana

facts.statement: In early July 1987, volunteer Sidney M. Hostetter found a horned dinosaur skull (specimen MOR 485) near the Canyon Bone Bed.
facts.quote: During the field season of 1987 (early July), volunteer Sidney M. Hostetter located another horned dinosaur skull near the Canyon Bone Bed, specimen MOR 485

facts.statement: In June 1989, Horner and his team discovered a subadult horned dinosaur skull and skeleton (specimen MOR 591) near Blacktail Creek.
facts.quote: At the end of June 1989, Horner, his son Jason and his head preparator Carrie Ancell discovered horned dinosaur specimen MOR 591, a subadult skull and partial postcranial skeleton, near the Blacktail Creek

facts.statement: Graduate student Scott D. Sampson joined the excavation team in the summer of 1989.
facts.quote: In the summer of 1989, graduate student Scott D. Sampson joined the team

facts.statement: The informal name "Styracosaurus makeli" appeared in a book by Stephen Czerkas in 1990 as an invalid nomen nudum.
facts.quote: In 1990, this name, as an invalid nomen nudum, appeared in a photo caption in a book by Stephen Czerkas

facts.statement: The genus Achelousaurus was named in 1994 by Sampson during a talk at the Society of Vertebrate Paleontology.
facts.quote: In 1994, in a talk during the annual meeting of the Society of Vertebrate Paleontology, he named "Taxon C" as a new genus and species, Achelousaurus horneri.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen for Achelousaurus horneri, designated MOR 485, was officially indicated in a 1995 article by Sampson.
facts.quote: In 1995, in a subsequent article, Sampson indicated specimen MOR 485 as the holotype specimen of Achelousaurus horneri.

facts.statement: The generic name Achelousaurus combines the Greek river deity Achelous with the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name consists of the words Achelous, the name of a Greek mythological figure, and saurus, which is Latinized Greek for lizard.

facts.statement: The specific name horneri honors paleontologist Jack Horner for his research on dinosaurs in Montana.
facts.quote: The specific name honors Jack Horner, for his research on the dinosaurs of the Two Medicine Formation in Montana.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was collected by Hostetter and Ray Rogers from the Landslide Butte Field Area, approximately 40 km northwest of Cut Bank.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen MOR 485 was collected by Hostetter and Ray Rogers from the Landslide Butte Field Area about 40 km northwest of Cut Bank.

facts.statement: Sampson described the holotype in 1995 as a partial skull of an adult containing nasal and supraorbital bosses and parietal bones.
facts.quote: In 1995 Sampson described it as the partial skull of an adult animal including the nasal and supraorbital (region above the eye socket) bosses (roundish protuberances instead of horns), and the parietal bones.

facts.statement: In 2015, Leonardo Maiorino reported that a fragmentary lower jaw catalogued as MOR 485-7-12-87-4 belongs to the holotype specimen.
facts.quote: In 2015, Leonardo Maiorino reported that as part of the same specimen a fragmentary lower jaw has been catalogued as MOR 485-7-12-87-4.

facts.statement: Two additional specimens collected 35 km south of Cut Bank on Blacktail Creek were referred to Achelousaurus by Sampson in 1995.
facts.quote: Two other specimens were collected on the Blacktail Creek, 35 km to the south of Cut Bank and referred to Achelousaurus by Sampson in 1995.

facts.statement: Specimen MOR 591 is a sub-adult skeleton that is about 60% complete, including the vertebral column, pelvis, sacrum, and femur.
facts.quote: Specimen MOR 591 is a partial skull and an about 60% complete skeleton of a sub-adult specimen that includes the vertebral column, pelvis, sacrum and a femur.

facts.statement: Specimen MOR 571 consists of a partial skull, lower jaws, ribs, and vertebrae belonging to an adult individual.
facts.quote: Specimen MOR 571 includes a partial skull and lower jaws with associated ribs and vertebrae of an adult.

facts.statement: A fifth specimen, MOR 456.1, is identified as a subadult individual.
facts.quote: A fifth specimen is MOR 456.1, a subadult.

facts.statement: None of the known Achelousaurus specimens represent advanced adult individuals.
facts.quote: None of the specimens were of an advanced individual age.

facts.statement: Andrew McDonald and colleagues concluded that the Achelousaurus fossils represent single individuals rather than bone beds.
facts.quote: According to Andrew McDonald and colleagues, the Achelousaurus finds represented single individuals, not bone beds.

facts.statement: In 2006, researchers proposed that the dubious species Monoclonius lowei could be a sub-adult of Styracosaurus, Achelousaurus, or Einiosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2006, it was also proposed that Monoclonius lowei, a dubious species based on a skull (specimen CMN 8790) from the Dinosaur Park Formation, could be a sub-adult specimen of Styracosaurus, Achelousaurus or Einiosaurus, with which it is roughly contemporaneous.

facts.statement: Indeterminate specimens from the Two Medicine Formation, including skull MOR 464 and snout MOR 449, may belong to Achelousaurus, Einiosaurus, or Styracosaurus ovatus.
facts.quote: In addition, some indeterminate specimens from the Two Medicine Formation – such as fragmentary skull MOR 464 or snout MOR 449 – may belong to Achelousaurus or the two other roughly contemporary ceratopsids Einiosaurus and Styracosaurus ovatus.

facts.statement: While MOR 591 was assigned to Achelousaurus in 1995, John Wilson and Jack Scannella suggested in 2021 that it might actually belong to Einiosaurus.
facts.quote: The subadult specimen MOR 591 was assigned to Achelousaurus in 1995 and henceforward, but in 2021, John Wilson and Jack Scannella stated that it could also possibly belong to Einiosaurus.

facts.statement: Achelousaurus is estimated to have reached a length of 6 meters and a weight of 3 metric tons.
facts.quote: Achelousaurus is estimated to have been 6 m long with a weight of 3 MT.

facts.statement: The skull of an adult Achelousaurus, represented by the holotype, was estimated to be 1.62 meters long.
facts.quote: The skull of an adult individual (holotype specimen MOR 485) was estimated to have been 1.62 m long.

facts.statement: Achelousaurus was similar in size to its relative Einiosaurus but possessed a much heavier build.
facts.quote: It was about as large as its close relative Einiosaurus, but with a much heavier build.

facts.statement: Achelousaurus exhibited a robustness approaching that of the large, heavily built Triceratops.
facts.quote: Achelousaurus approached the robustness of one of the largest and most heavily built horned dinosaurs known: Triceratops.

facts.statement: Achelousaurus had a large head with a hooked upper beak, large nasal openings, and dental batteries containing hundreds of stacked teeth.
facts.quote: Its very large head, which would have rested on a straight neck, had a hooked upper beak, very large nasal openings, and long tooth rows developed into dental batteries that contained hundreds of appressed and stacked individual teeth.

facts.statement: Each upper jaw bone of Achelousaurus contained 25 to 28 tooth positions arranged in dental batteries.
facts.quote: Achelousaurus had 25 to 28 such tooth positions in each maxilla (upper jaw bone).

facts.statement: Adult Achelousaurus individuals possess nasal bosses that are relatively small, thin, and heavily covered with pits.
facts.quote: Firstly, adult individuals have nasal bones with a boss on top that is relatively small and thin, and heavily covered with pits;

facts.statement: Adult Achelousaurus individuals lack true horns above the eye sockets, instead having large bosses with high ridges.
facts.quote: secondly, adult individuals do not have true horns above the eye sockets but relatively large bosses with high ridges;

facts.statement: Subadult Achelousaurus individuals possess true horncores above the eye sockets with a concave inward-facing surface.
facts.quote: thirdly, not yet fully grown individuals, or subadults, have true horncores (the bony part of the horns) above the eye sockets with the inward facing surface being concave;

facts.statement: The neck shield of Achelousaurus features a single pair of curved spikes extending from the rear margin outward and backward.
facts.quote: fourthly, the parietal bones of the neck shield have a single pair of curved spikes sticking out from the rear margin to behind and to the outside.

facts.statement: The frill spikes of Achelousaurus are more outwardly oriented compared to the medially curved spikes of Einiosaurus.
facts.quote: The frill spikes of Achelousaurus are more outwards oriented than the spikes of Einiosaurus, which are medially curved;

facts.statement: Achelousaurus differs from Pachyrhinosaurus by having a smaller nasal boss that does not extend to the rear of the frontal bones.
facts.quote: Achelousaurus also differs from Pachyrhinosaurus in its smaller nasal boss that does not reach the frontal bones at its rear.

facts.statement: Achelousaurus lived during the Campanian age as a member of the Centrosaurinae subgroup of ceratopsians.
facts.quote: This puts it in the same size-range as other members of the Centrosaurinae subgroup of ceratopsians that lived during the Campanian age.

facts.statement: Adult Achelousaurus skulls featured a rough, heavily pitted boss on the snout instead of a horn found in many other ceratopsids.
facts.quote: Adult Achelousaurus skulls had a rugose, heavily pitted boss on the snout or nasal region, where many other ceratopsids had a horn.

facts.statement: Adult Achelousaurus skulls possessed large, rough, oval bosses above the eyes rather than the horns seen in other ceratopsids.
facts.quote: Adult skulls also possess large, rugose, and oval bosses on the supraorbital region above the eyes, instead of the horns of other ceratopsids.

facts.statement: In Achelousaurus, the squamosal bone was significantly shorter than the parietal bone.
facts.quote: In Achelousaurus, the squamosal bone was much shorter than the parietal.

facts.statement: The neck shield of Achelousaurus featured two prominent large spikes that pointed backward and curved outward to the sides.
facts.quote: The frill of Achelousaurus had two conspicuous large spikes that were directed backwards and curved to the sides away from each other.

facts.statement: Paleontologists proposed that the rough bosses of Achelousaurus were covered by thick pads of keratinized skin, similar to the bosses of modern muskoxen.
facts.quote: They proposed that the rugose bosses of Achelousaurus and Pachyrhinosaurus were covered by thick pads of cornified (or keratinized) skin, similar to the boss of modern muskoxen (Ovibos moschatus).

facts.statement: In 1992, Horner et al. studied fossils from the upper Two Medicine Formation, noting a rapid succession of animal communities within about half a million years.
facts.quote: In 1992, the study by Horner et al. tried to account for the fact that within a limited geological period of time (about half a million years) there had been a quick succession of animal communities in the upper Two Medicine Formation.

facts.statement: Horner proposed that the succession of fossils represented anagenesis, where later forms were simply evolved versions of earlier ones rather than distinct species.
facts.quote: This suggested to him that he had discovered a rare proof of evolution in action: the later fauna was basically the old one but at a more evolved stage.

facts.statement: Horner argued that the different horned dinosaur types found were not separate species but transitional forms resulting from anagenesis.
facts.quote: The various types found were not distinct species but transitional forms developed within a process of anagenesis.

facts.statement: Horner identified "Transitional Taxon A" in layers 60 meters below the Bearpaw Formation, which he considered identical to Styracosaurus albertensis except for having only one pair of parietal spikes.
facts.quote: In the lowest layers of the Two Medicine Formation, 60 m below the overlaying Bearpaw Formation, "Transitional Taxon A" was present. It seemed to be identical to Styracosaurus albertensis, differing from it only in the possession of just a single pair of parietal spikes.

facts.statement: "Transitional Taxon B" was found in layers 45 meters below the Bearpaw Formation, characterized by a single pair of spikes and a nasal horn curving forward over the nasal bone branches.
facts.quote: The middle layers, 45 m below the Bearpaw, contained "Transitional Taxon B" that also had a single spike pair but differed in the form of its nasal horn that curved to the front over the anterior branches of the nasal bones.

facts.statement: "Transitional Taxon C" was discovered in strata 20 meters below the Bearpaw Formation, featuring a spike pair and a nasal horn fused with the front branches.
facts.quote: In the upper strata, 20 m below the Bearpaw, "Transitional Taxon C" had been excavated. It too had a spike pair but now the nasal horn was fused with the front branches.

facts.statement: Horner's three transitional taxa were subsequently named Stellasaurus, Einiosaurus, and Achelousaurus.
facts.quote: Subsequently, "Taxon A" was named Stellasaurus, "Taxon B" became Einiosaurus, while "Taxon C" became Achelousaurus.

facts.statement: These animals lived on a narrow coastal strip on the east coast of Laramidia, bordered by the Western Interior Seaway and the 3 to 4 km high proto-Rocky Mountains.
facts.quote: The animals were living on a narrow strip on the east-coast of Laramidia, bordering the Western Interior Seaway and constrained in the west by the 3 to 4 km high proto-Rocky Mountains.

facts.statement: Achelousaurus lived during the phase when the coastal habitat was at its narrowest, experiencing the strongest selection pressures.
facts.quote: This led to stronger selection pressures, the severest for Achelousaurus which lived during the phase that the coastal strip was at its narrowest.

facts.statement: The reduced habitat size caused a population bottleneck, which Horner suggested made rapid evolution possible.
facts.quote: The lower number of individuals that the smaller habitat could have sustained constituted a population bottleneck, making rapid evolution possible.

facts.statement: Horner hypothesized that increased sexual selection drove changes in sexual ornamentation like spikes, horns, and bosses.
facts.quote: Increased sexual selection would have induced changes in the sexual ornamentation such as spikes, horns and bosses.

facts.statement: In 1995, Sampson revised the timeline, estimating 860,000 years passed after the Brachyceratops quarry and 640,000 years after the Einiosaurus beds, contradicting Horner's shorter timeframe.
facts.quote: Basing himself on revised data, Sampson in 1995 estimated that the layers investigated represented a longer period of time than the initially assumed 500,000 years: after the deposition of Gilmore's Brachyceratops quarry, 860,000 years would have passed, and after the Einiosaurus beds 640,000 years, until the maximal extent of the Bearpaw transgression.

facts.statement: In 1996, Dodson objected to Horner's hypothesis, noting that having only one pair of main spikes was more basal than the three pairs seen in Styracosaurus albertensis.
facts.quote: In 1996, Dodson raised two objections to Horner's hypothesis. Firstly, the possession of just one pair of main spikes seemed more basal than the presence of three pairs, as with Styracosaurus albertensis.

facts.statement: In 2010, Horner admitted that specimen TMP 2002.76.1 suggested Achelousaurus was not descended from Einiosaurus because it was older but possessed a nasal boss.
facts.quote: In 2010, Horner admitted that specimen TMP 2002.76.1 seemed to indicate that Achelousaurus was not descended from Einiosaurus, as it preceded both in age, and yet had a nasal boss.

facts.statement: Wilson and colleagues attributed the differences between Einiosaurus and Achelousaurus to heterochrony, or differential development speeds of traits during an individual's lifetime.
facts.quote: The differences between the two taxa would have been caused by heterochrony – differential changes in the speed the various traits developed during the lifetime of an individual.

facts.statement: In 2020, Wilson and colleagues found Stellasaurus intermediate between Styracosaurus and Einiosaurus in morphology and stratigraphy, supporting its role in an anagenetic lineage.
facts.quote: Since Wilson and colleagues found in 2020 that Stellasaurus (Horner's "Taxon A") was intermediate between Styracosaurus and Einiosaurus in morphology and stratigraphy, they could not discount that it was a transitional taxon within an anagenetic lineage.

facts.statement: In 1995, Sampson formally classified Achelousaurus within the Ceratopsidae family, specifically the Centrosaurinae subfamily.
facts.quote: In 1995, Sampson formally placed Achelousaurus in the Ceratopsidae, more precisely the Centrosaurinae.

facts.statement: All analyses place both Einiosaurus and Achelousaurus within the clade Pachyrhinosaurini.
facts.quote: In all analyses, Einiosaurus and Achelousaurus are part of the clade Pachyrhinosaurini.

facts.statement: Achelousaurus is defined as a member of the clade Pachyrostra, or "thick-snouts," alongside Pachyrhinosaurus.
facts.quote: By definition, Achelousaurus is a member of the clade Pachyrostra (or "thick-snouts"), in which it is united with Pachyrhinosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul assigned Achelousaurus horneri to the genus Centrosaurus, but this classification has not been accepted by other researchers who consistently retain the name Achelousaurus.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul assigned A. horneri to the genus Centrosaurus, as C. horneri. This has found no acceptance among other researchers, with subsequent taxonomic assessments invariably keeping the generic name Achelousaurus.

facts.statement: All phylogenetic analyses identify Achelousaurus and Pachyrhinosaurus as sister groups.
facts.quote: In all analyses, Achelousaurus and Pachyrhinosaurus were sister groups.

facts.statement: Achelousaurus is considered the most basal member of the clade Pachyrostra.
facts.quote: Achelousaurus is the basalmost pachyrostran.

facts.statement: The clade Pachyrostra is defined by enlarged nasal ornamentation and the transformation of nasal and brow horns into bosses.
facts.quote: Shared derived traits (or synapomorphies) of the group are an enlarged nasal ornamentation and a change of the nasal and brow horns into bosses.

facts.statement: Scientists debate whether Styracosaurus albertensis or Einiosaurus was the direct ancestor of Achelousaurus.
facts.quote: Subsequent studies have sought to determine the precise relationships within this part of the evolutionary tree, with conflicting results regarding the question whether Styracosaurus albertensis or Einiosaurus might have been in the direct line of ascent to Achelousaurus.

facts.statement: The clade Pachyrhinosaurini was established in 2012 to include species closer to Achelousaurus and Pachyrhinosaurus than to Centrosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2012, the clade Pachyrhinosaurini was named, consisting of species more closely related to Pachyrhinosaurus or Achelousaurus than to Centrosaurus.

facts.statement: Research in 2009 suggested Achelousaurus used its nasal and supraorbital bosses for butting or ramming rivals during combat.
facts.quote: Hieronymus, in 2009, concluded that the nasal and supraorbital bosses were used for butting or ramming the head or the flank of a rival.

facts.statement: The bosses of Achelousaurus were likely covered in cornified pads, indicating dominance fights similar to modern muskoxen.
facts.quote: The bone structure indicates that the bosses were covered by cornified pads as in modern muskoxen, suggesting dominance fights similar to those of members of the Caprinae subfamily.

facts.statement: The evolution of bosses in Centrosaurinae reflects a shift in fighting technique from clashing horns to high-energy head-butting.
facts.quote: The evolution from horncores into bosses in Centrosaurinae would likewise have reflected a change in fighting technique, from clashing to high-energy head-butting.

facts.statement: All three main Achelousaurus specimens possess three fused neck vertebrae, a trait possibly inherited from ancestors that used stiffer necks for burrowing or feeding.
facts.quote: All three main known specimens have syncervicals consisting of three fused neck vertebrae; the trait could have been inherited from a smaller ancestor using a stiffer neck for burrowing or food acquisition.

facts.statement: Researcher Dodson concluded that monospecific Achelousaurus bone beds confirm these dinosaurs lived in herds.
facts.quote: Dodson concluded that the fact that the Achelousaurus bone beds were monospecific (containing only one species) confirmed the existence of herds.

facts.statement: Oxygen isotope analysis of Achelousaurus bones suggests they were homeothermic endotherms.
facts.quote: The variation of the dinosaurs, including MOR 591, was consistent with them being homeothermic endotherms.

facts.statement: Achelousaurus likely had an intermediate metabolic rate, lower than modern mammals and birds but higher than ectotherms.
facts.quote: The metabolic rate of these dinosaurs was likely not as high as that of modern mammals and birds, and they may have been intermediate endotherms.

facts.statement: If specimen MOR 591 belongs to Achelousaurus, the genus may have reached adult size faster than Einiosaurus, as it was the same size as a larger Einiosaurus skull but younger.
facts.quote: In 2021 a study by Wilson and Scannella pointed out that specimen MOR 591 was of a younger individual age than the Einiosaurus skull MOR 456 8-8-87-1, but of the same size. If MOR 591 could indeed be referred to Achelousaurus, this might indicate this genus reached its adult size more quickly.

facts.statement: Achelousaurus lived between 83 and 74 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Achelousaurus is known from the Two Medicine Formation, which preserves coastal sediments dating from the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous Period, between 83 and 74 million years ago.

facts.statement: Achelousaurus lived in a warm semiarid climate.
facts.quote: The Two Medicine Formation is typified by a warm semiarid climate.

facts.statement: A 2013 study determined that Achelousaurus was restricted to feeding on vegetation no higher than 1 meter.
facts.quote: Achelousaurus ate much smaller plants, though: a 2013 study determined that ceratopsid herbivores on Laramidia were restricted to feeding on vegetation with a height of 1 m or lower.

facts.statement: Tooth marks on fossils suggest that a large theropod predator, possibly Albertosaurus, scavenged Achelousaurus remains.
facts.quote: As proven by tooth marks, horned dinosaur fossils in the Landslide Butte Field Area had been scavenged by a large theropod predator, which Rogers suggested were Albertosaurus.

facts.statement: The first fossils of Achelousaurus were collected in Montana in 1987 by a team led by Jack Horner, with further finds made in 1989.
facts.quote: Los primeros fósiles de Achelousaurus fueron recolectados en Montana en 1987 , por un equipo dirigido por Jack Horner, con más hallazgos realizados en 1989.

facts.statement: Achelousaurus horneri was described and named by Scott D. Sampson in 1994.
facts.quote: En 1994, Achelousaurus horneri fue descrito y nombrado por Scott D. Sampson

facts.statement: Achelousaurus could measure about 6 meters in length and weigh about 3 tons.
facts.quote: Siendo un gran centrosaurino, Achelousaurus podría medir unos 6 metros de largo, con un peso de unas 3 toneladas.

facts.statement: Achelousaurus had a bony frill on the back of its skull featuring a pair of long spikes that curved outward.
facts.quote: Tenía un volante óseo en el cuello en la parte posterior del cráneo, que lucía un par de púas largas, que se curvaban hacia el exterior.

facts.statement: Adult Achelousaurus had rounded bumps over the eyes and snout where other centrosaurines often had horns.
facts.quote: Un Achelousaurus adulto tenía protuberancias redondeadas sobre los ojos y en el hocico donde otros centrosaurinos a menudo tenían cuernos en las mismas posiciones.

facts.statement: Some researchers hypothesize that the bumps on Achelousaurus were used in head-butting fights and for display.
facts.quote: Algunos investigadores plantean la hipótesis de que las protuberancias se usaban en peleas, con los animales dándose cabezazos, así como para exhibición.

facts.statement: Within Ceratopsia, Achelousaurus belongs to the clade Pachyrostra, or "thick-snouts".
facts.quote: Dentro de los Ceratopsia, Achelousaurus se encuentra dentro del clado Pachyrostra u "hocicos gruesos".

facts.statement: There has been debate regarding Achelousaurus's ancestry, with later discoveries showing it is closely related to Pachyrhinosaurus in the group Pachyrhinosaurini.
facts.quote: Ha habido debate sobre esta teoría, con descubrimientos posteriores que muestran que Achelousaurus está estrechamente relacionado con Pachyrhinosaurus en el grupo Pachyrhinosaurini.

facts.statement: The genus authority for Achelousaurus is Sampson, 1995.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Sampson, 1995

facts.statement: The species authority for Achelousaurus horneri is Sampson, 1995.
facts.quote: species_authority: Sampson, 1995

facts.statement: Achelousaurus lived at the end of the Cretaceous Period, approximately 75 million years ago, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 75 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Achelousaurus grew to approximately 6 meters in length and nearly 3 meters in height, though its weight remains unknown.
facts.quote: Achelousaurus llegó a medir alrededor de 6 metros de largo y casi 3 de alto, con un peso, por ahora, desconocido.

facts.statement: The animal was characterized by bone bumps on its snout and a pair of horns on its bony frill.
facts.quote: Se caracterizaba por presentar unas protuberancias óseas en el hocico y un par de cuernos en su volante óseo.

facts.statement: The skull of a mature Achelousaurus, including the frill horns, measured 1.6 meters in length.
facts.quote: El cráneo de un Achelousaurus maduro, incluyendo los cuernos de la gola, media 1,6 metros de largo.

facts.statement: It possessed a beak very similar to that of a modern parrot, but larger.
facts.quote: Tenía un pico muy parecido al de un loro actual, pero más grande.

facts.statement: Like other family members, it had a bony plate surrounding its neck, topped by two long horns.
facts.quote: Como todos los miembros de su familia, tenía una placa ósea rodeando su cuello, coronada por dos largos cuernos.

facts.statement: It also had bumps around its mouth and behind its eyes.
facts.quote: También poseía protuberancias alrededor de su boca y detrás de sus ojos.

facts.statement: Estimates suggest Achelousaurus measured 6 meters in length and weighed 3 tonnes.
facts.quote: Se estima que Achelousaurus medía 6 metros de largo y pesaba 3 toneladas.

facts.statement: The skull of an adult individual, the holotype specimen MOR 485, is estimated to have been 1.62 meters long.
facts.quote: Se estima que el cráneo de un individuo adulto, espécimen holotipo MOR 485 medía 1,62 metros de largo.

facts.statement: It was nearly as large as its close relative Einiosaurus but had a much heavier build.
facts.quote: Era casi tan grande como su pariente cercano Einiosaurus, pero con una constitución mucho más pesada.

facts.statement: As a ceratopsian, Achelousaurus would have been a quadruped with hoofed toes and a shortened tail curved downward.
facts.quote: Como ceratópsido, Achelousaurus habría sido un animal cuadrúpedo con dedos ungulados y una cola acortada y curvada hacia abajo.

facts.statement: Its large head, resting on a straight neck, featured a hooked upper beak, very large nasal openings, and long rows of teeth developed into dental batteries containing hundreds of tightly stacked individual teeth.
facts.quote: Su cabeza muy grande, que habría descansado sobre un cuello recto, tenía un pico superior ganchudo, aberturas nasales muy grandes y largas filas de dientes que se desarrollaron en baterías dentales que contenían cientos de dientes individuales apretados y apilados.

facts.statement: New teeth grew beneath old ones in the dental sockets, with each position holding a column of teeth stacked one over the other.
facts.quote: En los alvéolos dentales, crecían dientes nuevos debajo de los viejos, cada posición albergaba una columna de dientes colocados uno sobre el otro.

facts.statement: Achelousaurus had between 25 and 28 positions for these teeth in each upper jaw.
facts.quote: Achelousaurus tenía entre 25 y 28 posiciones de dientes de este tipo en cada maxilar superior.

facts.statement: In 1995, Sampson provided a formal list of four traits distinguishing Achelousaurus from its centrosaurine relatives when describing the species.
facts.quote: En 1995, al describir la especie, Sampson dio una lista formal de cuatro rasgos que distinguen a Achelousaurus de sus parientes centrosaurinos.

facts.statement: First, adult individuals have nasal bones with a relatively small, thin bump on top that is heavily covered in holes.
facts.quote: En primer lugar, los individuos adultos tienen huesos nasales con una protuberancia en la parte superior que es relativamente pequeña y delgada, y está muy cubierta de hoyos.

facts.statement: Second, adult individuals do not have true horns over the eye sockets, but rather relatively large bumps with high ridges.
facts.quote: En segundo lugar, los individuos adultos no tienen cuernos verdaderos sobre las cuencas de los ojos, sino protuberancias relativamente grandes con crestas altas.

facts.statement: Third, individuals that have not fully grown, or subadults, have true bony cores of horns over the eye sockets with the inward-facing surface being concave.
facts.quote: En tercer lugar, los individuos que aún no han crecido completamente, o subadultos, tienen verdaderos núcleos córneo, la parte ósea de los cuernos, sobre las cuencas de los ojos con la superficie que mira hacia adentro siendo cóncava.

facts.statement: Fourth, the parietal bones of the neck shield have a single pair of curved spikes protruding from the rear margin backward and outward.
facts.quote: Y en cuarto lugar, los huesos parietales del escudo del cuello tienen un solo par de púas curvas que sobresalen del margen posterior hacia atrás y hacia afuera.

facts.statement: However, the spikes of Achelousaurus are less directed outward than the comparable spikes of Pachyrhinosaurus.
facts.quote: las púas de Achelousaurus están, sin embargo, menos dirigidas hacia el exterior que las púas comparables de Pachyrhinosaurus.

facts.statement: Achelousaurus also differs from Pachyrhinosaurus by having a smaller nasal bump that does not reach the frontal bones at the back.
facts.quote: Achelousaurus también se diferencia de Pachyrhinosaurus en su protuberancia nasal más pequeña que no alcanza los huesos frontales en su parte posterior.

facts.statement: Aside from the skull, no skeletal features are known that distinguish Achelousaurus from other members of the Centrosaurinae.
facts.quote: Aparte del cráneo, no se conocen características del esqueleto que distingan a Achelousaurus de otros miembros de los Centrosaurinae.

facts.statement: Achelousaurus exhibited the constitution of derived, "advanced" centrosaurines, characterized by short frontal horns or bumps combined with elaborate frill spikes.
facts.quote: Achelousaurus exhibió la constitución de los centrosaurinos derivados, "avanzados", que se caracterizan por cuernos o protuberancias frontales cortas, combinadas con elaboradas púas en el volante.

facts.statement: The general proportions of the frill are typically centrosaurine, with a wide, rounded squamosal bone on the side that expands toward the rear.
facts.quote: Las proporciones generales del volante son típicamente centrosaurino, con un hueso escamoso ancho y redondeado en el costado, que se expande hacia la parte posterior.

facts.statement: It also shares the typical frill curvature with a top surface that is convex from side to side and concave from front to back.
facts.quote: También comparte la curvatura típica del volante con una superficie superior que es convexa de lado a lado y cóncava de adelante hacia atrás.

facts.statement: All known specimens of Achelousaurus were recovered from the Two Medicine Formation in Glacier County, Montana, during excavations by the Museum of the Rockies, which still houses the specimens.
facts.quote: Todos los especímenes conocidos de Achelousaurus fueron recuperados de la Formación Two Medicine en el condado de Glacier, Montana, durante las excavaciones realizadas por el Museo de las Montañas Rocosas, que aún alberga los especímenes.

facts.statement: In August 1985, Horner's associate Bob Makela discovered a rich fossil deposit on farmer Ricky Reagan's land, called Dinosaur Ridge Quarry, containing ceratopsian fossils.
facts.quote: En agosto de 1985, el asociado de Horner, Bob Makela, descubrió un rico yacimiento de fósiles en la tierra del granjero Ricky Reagan, que se llamó Dinosaur Ridge Quarry y contenía fósiles de dinosaurios con cuernos.

facts.statement: In late June 1989, Horner, his son Jason, and chief preparer Carrie Ancell discovered ceratopsian specimen MOR 591, a subadult skull and partial postcranial skeleton, near Blacktail Creek.
facts.quote: A fines de junio de 1989, Horner, su hijo Jason y su preparador principal Carrie Ancell descubrieron el espécimen de dinosaurio con cuernos MOR 591, un cráneo subadulto y un esqueleto postcraneal parcial, cerca de Blacktail Creek.

facts.statement: This places it in the same size range as other members of the Centrosaurinae ceratopsian subgroup that lived during the Campanian age.
facts.quote: Esto lo coloca en el mismo rango de tamaño que otros miembros del subgrupo Centrosaurinae de ceratopsianos que vivieron durante la era Campaniense.

facts.statement: A cladogram by Wilson and colleagues in 2020 shows the phylogenetic position of Achelousaurus.
facts.quote: El cladograma a continuación muestra la posición filogenética de Achelousaurus en un cladograma de Wilson y colegas en 2020.

facts.statement: In 1995, Sampson noted that earlier studies suggested ceratopsian horns and frills likely functioned in intraspecific display and combat.
facts.quote: En 1995, Sampson señaló que estudios anteriores habían encontrado que los cuernos y volantes de los ceratopsianos probablemente tenían una función en la exhibición y el combate intraespecífico

facts.statement: In 1995, Sampson rejected the possibility that skull ornamentation differences between Einiosaurus and Achelousaurus represented sexual dimorphism, citing three reasons.
facts.quote: Sampson en 1995 rechazó la posibilidad de que la diferencia en la ornamentación del cráneo entre Einiosaurus y Achelousaurus representara dimorfismo sexual, por tres razones

facts.statement: In 2009, Hieronymus concluded that nasal and supraorbital protuberances were used to strike or butt an opponent's head or flank.
facts.quote: En 2009, Hieronymus concluyó que las protuberancias nasales y supraorbitales se usaban para golpear o embestir la cabeza o el flanco de un rival

facts.statement: Bone structure indicates the protuberances were covered by keratinous pads similar to those of modern muskoxen.
facts.quote: La estructura ósea indica que las protuberancias estaban cubiertas por almohadillas cornificadas como en los bueyes almizcleros modernos

facts.statement: Head-butting would have been a costly and risky behavior for these dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Los cabezazos habrían sido un comportamiento costoso y arriesgado

facts.statement: Previously, the fusion of the first three neck vertebrae seen in the mature MOR 571 specimen was suggested to be a paleopathology.
facts.quote: Anteriormente se había sugerido que la fusión de las tres primeras vértebras del cuello, como se ve en el espécimen maduro MOR 571, podría haber sido una paleopatología

facts.statement: However, in 1997 it was concluded that the fused neck vertebrae forming a 'sincervical' were likely a normal ontogenetic trait to support the heavy head.
facts.quote: pero en 1997 se concluyó que era más probable que fuera un rasgo ontogenético normal, las vértebras creciendo juntas para formar un llamado "sincervical" para sostener la cabeza pesada

facts.statement: The three main known specimens possess sincervicals consisting of three fused neck vertebrae.
facts.quote: Los tres especímenes principales conocidos tienen sincervicales que consisten en tres vértebras del cuello fusionadas

facts.statement: This trait may have been inherited from a smaller ancestor that used a stiffer neck to dig or acquire food.
facts.quote: el rasgo podría haber sido heredado de un ancestro más pequeño que usaba un cuello más rígido para excavar o adquirir alimentos

facts.statement: It has been claimed that ceratopsian dinosaurs were herd animals due to numerous bone beds containing multiple individuals of the same species.
facts.quote: Se ha afirmado que los dinosaurios ceratopsianos eran animales de manada, debido a la gran cantidad de lechos óseos conocidos que contienen múltiples miembros de la misma especie de ceratopsiano

facts.statement: Horner assumed that horned dinosaurs at Landslide Butte lived in herds that died due to drought or disease.
facts.quote: Horner asumió que los dinosaurios con cuernos en Landslide Butte vivían en manadas que habían muerto por sequía o enfermedad

facts.statement: Dodson concluded that the monospecific nature of Achelousaurus bone beds confirmed the existence of herds.
facts.quote: Dodson concluyó que el hecho de que los lechos óseos de Achelousaurus fueran monoespecíficos (que contenían solo una especie) confirmaba la existencia de manadas

facts.statement: The genus Achelousaurus was named by Sampson in 1994.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Achelousaurus (genus), Sampson 1994

facts.statement: The parent group of Achelousaurus is Pachyrhinosaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Pachyrhinosaurini

facts.statement: Achelousaurus belongs to the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Family: Ceratopsidae

facts.statement: Achelousaurus is classified within the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Achelousaurus is Achelousaurus horneri.
facts.quote: Type species: Achelousaurus horneri

facts.statement: Achelousaurus lived during the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are two recorded fossil occurrences of Achelousaurus in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 2
